abstract: Maintains en-route satellite telemetry signal reliability and comm relay status
system_message:
You are Aeronautical Telemetry Specialist (TEL). As the Aeronautical Telemetry Specialist (TEL), you maintain en-route satellite telemetry signal reliability and communications relay status across high-altitude evacuation routes, tracking continuous telemetry track link availability and direct cockpit-to-hospital voice link latency.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Satellite voice latency（LATN）
information_points.content:
TEL-LATN-RUN：For the Valley River Low-Altitude Transit, voice link round-trip latency over the direct cockpit-to-hospital satellite link averages 220 ms during emergency voice transmissions.
TEL-LATN-RBR：For the Southern Crest Ridge Bypass, voice link round-trip latency over the direct cockpit-to-hospital satellite link averages 460 ms for digital voice communications.
TEL-LATN-ZCL：For the Glacier Pass High-Level Route, voice link round-trip latency over the direct cockpit-to-hospital satellite link averages 340 ms for high-frequency digital emergency voice communications.

information_points.title: Maintains en-route satellite telemetry signal reliability and comm relay status（COM）
information_points.content:
TEL-COM-XLK：For the Valley River Low-Altitude Transit, satellite telemetry link uptime across the continuous telemetry track stands at 99%, tracking unbroken bidirectional telemetry and biomedical data transmission.
TEL-COM-4ON：For the Glacier Pass High-Level Route, satellite telemetry link uptime across the continuous telemetry track is 96%, measuring unbroken bidirectional telemetry and biomedical data transmission.
TEL-COM-LKE：For the Southern Crest Ridge Bypass, satellite telemetry link uptime across the continuous telemetry track is recorded at 96%, reflecting unbroken bidirectional telemetry and biomedical data transmission.
